verdict: Avoid new iron & steel exposure in Bhilai for now; lend only to value-added, non-BSP-linked units with tight structure, and decline scrap-trading and single-buyer re-rollers.
title: Bhilai iron & steel: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Bhilai re-roller buys sponge iron, scrap and billet, melts and rolls it into TMT bars, structurals or billets, and sells into construction and BSP-linked supply chains.** Cash turns on the spread between input cost and finished price, not on volume alone. Fixed cost is furnace power and labour; working capital sits in inventory (scrap, billet, finished stock) and in receivables from traders and contractors. **The value sits in the conversion margin and in who you sell to, not in the tonnage.**

## What has changed now
**The data pack scores this cluster AVOID at 27, and the local signals are the reason.** Chhattisgarh GST collections grew +2.4% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, and state electricity demand +6.7% against India's +9.5% [D] — both slower than the country, which tells us local demand and local activity are lagging. **Brent at $113/bbl sits above the $75–100 band [D], so freight and power-linked costs stay high while local pricing power is weak.** India-wide IIP for NIC 24 is only +2.4% YoY [D].

## Local news versus peers
**The Bhilai news flow is about security and theft, not demand.** A CISF steel-sector security setup is being headquartered in Bhilai [1], and a 35-member CBI team is probing scrap theft at BSP [2]. Read that as a warning on scrap custody and collateral quality, not as a growth signal. **Peer results are strong but not local:** JSW Steel's Q2 FY27 net profit was Rs.5,279 crore against Rs.1,623 crore a year earlier [4], and Kirloskar Ferrous grew revenue 17% y-o-y to INR 2,046.7 crore while coking coal and rupee depreciation eroded margins [6]. **The rating reports are undated and generic** — ICRA on environmental and flood risk [8], CARE on SAIL liquidity [9], CRISIL on a BBB- re-roller [10] — so treat them as structure guidance, not Bhilai evidence.

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue value-added converters with diversified buyers:** units making structurals, galvanised or specialised sections, selling to more than one end-market, with own power or a fixed-tariff supply. **Avoid scrap traders, single-buyer re-rollers feeding only BSP, and any unit whose stock cannot be independently verified** — the scrap-theft probe [2] makes that a live risk. When a proposal lands, check the buyer mix and the top-three receivable concentration; if one buyer exceeds a third of sales, ask for the contract and a monthly sales register. **Structure on inventory and receivables, not on land.** Take monthly stock statements reconciled to GST returns, a receivables ageing, and power bills; if stock value falls below the drawing-power norm, ask for the shortfall in cash.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the local lag first.** If Chhattisgarh GST growth stays below India's +6.1% [D] for another quarter, tighten limits on trader-dependent units. If Brent stays above $113/bbl [D], ask each borrower for the power and freight cost line and test the margin at that cost. If a borrower's scrap supplier list changes sharply, ask why before renewing.
watch: State growth below India's +6.1% [D] for two quarters -> cut limits on trader-dependent units
Stock value below drawing-power norm -> demand cash shortfall or reduce limit
Units fall while sales rise -> ask for explanation, verify stock
Top buyer above one-third of sales -> seek contract, cap exposure
Above $113/bbl [D] -> re-test margin at that cost before renewal
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
